text:
No Cabs, No Clarity: Ola-Uber Drivers Extend Mumbai Strike, Airport Issues Travel Advisory
As app-based cab drivers rally for fair wages and stronger protections, Mumbai faces widespread travel chaos with little relief in sight.
Mumbai’s daily commuters are grappling with major transport delays yet again as Ola and Uber drivers continue their protest for a second consecutive day.
The strike, which began on July 15, has gained momentum with thousands of app-based drivers from across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) gathering at Azad Maidan near CSMT.
Recommended Stories
Why Are Drivers Protesting?
At the core of the protest is the demand for fare rationalisation in line with RTO-approved tariffs. Drivers say they earn just Rs 8–Rs 9 per kilometre, which they argue is not enough to cover rising fuel prices, vehicle maintenance, and loan repayments.
Protesters are also calling for:
- A ban on bike taxis like Rapido
- A cap on cab and auto permits to control oversupply
- Reinstatement of deactivated accounts
- A proper welfare board for drivers
- A fair grievance redressal system
“We’re being exploited. Ola and Uber charge high commissions and leave us with nothing," said a protesting driver, as per Free Press Journal.
Airport Advisory Issued
The situation has been especially tough for people heading to or from Mumbai Airport. The airport authority issued a public advisory on X, urging passengers to check for transport availability and make backup plans. Many travellers faced delays, missed rides, and last-minute hassles.
In light of ongoing protests in the state, passengers travelling via
[#MumbaiAirport]are advised to check transport availability and plan alternate arrangements in advance.[#CSMIA][#PassengerAdvisory][#Travel][#Aviation][pic.twitter.com/UnWScJue6U]— Mumbai Airport (@CSMIA_Official)[July 16, 2025]
Furthermore, commuters have shared disturbing accounts of ride disruptions. Rakesh Shah from Mulund said, “Protesters forced my driver to cancel mid-ride. It was frightening." Others reported being stranded for hours, as striking drivers blocked or threatened working ones.
What Lies Ahead?
Union leaders claim this was meant to be a one-day dharna, but protests spilled into Wednesday with no clear end in sight. They accuse the government of ignoring the Maharashtra Gig Workers’ Act and failing to take firm action on illegal operators.
